subject: Civil Engineering
title: Wind Load: The Invisible Force
description: A short lesson to help you apply Wind Load: The Invisible Force.

hook.text: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge twisted apart in 1940. The culprit? A 40 mph wind.

buildup.text: Wind pushes on a building's face, pulls on its back, and lifts on the roof.

discovery.text: Wind force grows with the square of speed — double the wind, four times the push.

twist.text: Tall buildings sway in wind on purpose — rigidity would make them crack.

climax.text: Taipei 101 uses a 730-ton pendulum to counteract wind sway at the top.

punchline.text: You can't see wind, but every tall building feels it.

quiz.question: How does wind force change when wind speed doubles?
options: It stays the same but changes direction

details.summary: Wind creates pressure on structures that varies with wind speed squared, building shape, height, and exposure. Windward faces experience positive pressure pushing inward, while leeward faces and roof surfaces experience suction pulling outward.
details.whyItMatters: Wind is a primary lateral force for most structures and the dominant design load for tall buildings, towers, and long-span bridges. Wind-induced failures can be sudden and catastrophic.
takeaways: Wind pressure increases with the square of wind speed and with building height
Suction on leeward faces and roofs often exceeds positive windward pressure
Tall buildings require aerodynamic shaping to reduce wind-induced oscillation

faq.question: Why do wind loads increase so rapidly with building height?
faq.answer: Wind speed increases with height because ground surface friction slows wind near the ground. At greater heights, this friction effect diminishes and wind speed approaches the free-stream gradient velocity.

faq.question: What causes tall buildings to sway in the wind?
faq.answer: Vortex shedding creates alternating low-pressure zones on opposite sides of the building as wind flows past, causing rhythmic side-to-side forces. If the shedding frequency matches the building's natural frequency, resonance amplifies the oscillation.
